comment: Repositories the heuristics have been measured against, pinned to the
commit they were measured at. Pinned so that a change to a rule can be
measured rather than argued about: the same trees, the same findings,
and a difference that means something. Chosen for what they contain, not
for fame -- between them they carry every format the tool reads, in five
programming languages, with a translated interface and a fixture tree.
The last two are deliberately vulnerable and measure the other
direction: what the rules fail to notice.

repositories.name: cli
repositories.for: a clean Go repository: the false-positive floor

repositories.name: dagger
repositories.for: composite actions, generated clients, documentation per release

repositories.name: discourse
repositories.for: Ruby, a translated interface, and a fixture full of one key

repositories.name: authentik
repositories.for: OAuth and SAML: identifiers named after passwords

repositories.name: n8n
repositories.for: TypeScript at scale: credential type names everywhere

repositories.name: ingress-nginx
repositories.for: Kubernetes at scale, and Go tests that skip verification

repositories.name: vault-helm
repositories.for: a Helm chart, templates and all

repositories.name: helm-charts
repositories.for: a hundred charts: templates, values, and the settings people really ship

repositories.name: grafana-operator
repositories.for: manifests, kustomize overlays, an operator SDK layout

repositories.name: terraform-aws-eks
repositories.for: a Terraform module written by people who know the rules

repositories.name: spring-petclinic
repositories.for: a small Maven project: the false-positive floor for Java

repositories.name: laravel
repositories.for: a PHP skeleton: small, and should stay silent
